question.problem:
Suppose we would like to find the minimum of the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}$ on the intersection of the surfaces ${y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4$ and $2x-y+{z}^{2}=4$ using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers $\lambda $ and $\mu $ satisfy the following system: 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}⟨2x,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}},\,-2z⟩=\lambda ⟨0,\,2y,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,⟩+\mu ⟨2,\,-1,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,⟩ \\ {y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4 \\ 2x-y+{z}^{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the expressions?
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the minimum value of 

$$
f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}
$$

 

subject to the constraints 

$$
g(x,y,z)={y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4,\,h(x,y,z)=2x-y+{z}^{2}=4.
$$

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ g(x,y,z)=4 \\ h(x,y,z)=4\end{aligned}
$$

We now expand the first equation of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x},{f}_{y},{f}_{z}⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x},{g}_{y},{g}_{z}⟩+\mu ⟨{h}_{x},{h}_{y},{h}_{z}⟩ \\ ⟨2x,\,4y,\,-2z⟩ & =\lambda ⟨0,\,2y,\,2z⟩+\mu ⟨2,\,-1,\,2z⟩\end{aligned}
$$
